picks.title: Suno inks global licensing deal with BMG
picks.excerpt: Suno's agreement with BMG covers recorded and publishing repertoire worldwide, following its Warner deal nine months earlier. Artists and songwriters must opt in before their work feeds the models.
picks.rationale: Suno's second major-label deal turns opt-in licensing into the working default for AI music, and MBW is the trade of record on it.

picks.title: Spotify has roped indie publisher Kobalt into its AI platform for covers and remixes
picks.excerpt: Spotify signed Kobalt for its forthcoming AI covers-and-remixes tool, a paid Premium add-on that lets fans generate their own versions of licensed songs. Participating writers get an extra royalty line.
picks.rationale: The first publisher outside Universal to clear fan-made AI remixes — songwriters now have a concrete opt-in and a new royalty line to decide on.

picks.title: Noizefield updates Audio Plugin Coder to v1.4.0 — JUCE 9 support, guided setup and AI workflow commands
picks.excerpt: Audio Plugin Coder is an open-source framework that turns a natural-language plugin concept into a buildable VST3/AU project using AI agents. v1.4.0 adds JUCE 9.0.1 support, a setup wizard and dedicated AI workflow commands.
picks.rationale: Most actionable item in the pool: a free, open-source path from a written plugin idea to a buildable VST3/AU, now with a guided setup.

picks.title: The Era of Unlabeled AI Content in Europe Is Ending
picks.excerpt: New EU AI Act transparency provisions took effect August 2, requiring AI-generated or AI-manipulated audio, images, video and text to be clearly identified as artificial. Non-compliance can draw fines of up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover.
picks.rationale: Replaces the CDM 'anti-bangers' pick, a re-run of a story already published 2026-08-06. Labeling is now a live obligation rather than a debate: every release touching AI in the EU has a disclosure question attached, and the penalty ceiling makes it a compliance line, not a norm.

picks.title: Where artists draw the line on AI: Uppbeat Creator Report
picks.excerpt: A survey of nearly 1,800 creative professionals found only 6.7% accept fully AI-generated content, while roughly 60% welcome AI as a collaborator. It maps where creators actually draw the assist-versus-replace line.
picks.rationale: Fresh numbers from ~1,800 working creatives that put a hard figure on the assist-versus-replace line everyone else is arguing about.

items.title: Music to confuse AI might be the next new genre
items.excerpt: Artists including MattstaGraham and iamriverhawk are deliberately writing 'anti-bangers' — deformed, unconventional tracks made in the hope that AI trains on them. Data poisoning is turning into an actual creative practice.
items.rationale: Data poisoning reframed as a compositional method — the rare AI story that hands musicians a new thing to make rather than a policy to obey.
